item.title: Pegasus Spyware Found on European Parliament PEGA Committee Member’s Phone
item.content:encoded:
Spyware found on phone of European Parliament member probing it — Should Read

Citizen Lab says former European Parliament member Stelios Kouloglou was infected with Pegasus spyware while serving on the committee investigating spyware abuse, including during key periods of its work. Researchers linked the targeting to the same Pegasus operator behind attacks on Russian and Belarusian journalists and opposition figures, underscoring concerns that commercial spyware is being used against democratic oversight.

  • Citizen Lab reported that former European Parliament member Stelios Kouloglou’s phone was infected with Pegasus spyware in October 2022 and again in March 2023 while he served on the PEGA Committee investigating spyware misuse.
  • The PEGA Committee was working on recommendations to address abuse of commercial spyware in Europe when the infections occurred, and it released those recommendations in May 2023.
  • Citizen Lab believes the same Pegasus customer was responsible for the Kouloglou infections and for attacks on seven Russian and Belarusian-speaking journalists and opposition figures between August 2020 and January 2023.
  • Kouloglou told Recorded Future News he believes the Greek government is responsible for the hacks, but Citizen Lab said it has no indications that this is true.
  • Hannah Neumann, a Green Party representative from Germany and PEGA Committee negotiator, said spying on a member of the European Parliament while he was investigating spyware abuse showed disregard for European democracy.
